Each time 'The Player' loops around it's main game loop, it will broadcast a 'tick' event which triggers here in each of the 'Level' sprite clones.

We Set the position to this Level sprite based on it's Offset and HALF of the Scroll X set by 'The Player' before it triggered this event.

If the real 'x position' of this sprite is the same as the value we requested it to be then it must be on the screen now and we show it, otherwise it must be offscreen and we hide it.

%LH0a39_2~!-%Zk3#!vS.text: Each costume of this sprite will be laid out as a screen sized tile, one after the other from left to right.  For this example I create '20' screens in a row (if you create more screens than you have costumes then they just loop around again.I use clones here, First setting the correct costume and Offset for the new sprite clone, and then calling the create clone block before setting up the next sprite to be cloned.Notice I offset each tile by 478 pixels.  A full screen is actually 480 pixels, but by reducing it by 2 pixels you remove any gap that can appear due to scratch scaling the project up to full screen size.
